common_name: Nina Witch Hazel (Vigorous Rounded Yellow Curly-Petaled Winter Shrub)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, humus-rich, slightly acidic soil in partial shade to full sun; 'Nina' matures into an unusually large, vigorous, well-rounded shrub, so allow it plenty of room to reach its full width.

directions: Nina is a large, robust hybrid witch hazel selection valued for its long, curling, deep yellow petals that open on bare branches in late winter and carry a light, sweet fragrance on mild days. It grows into an especially vigorous, rounded shrub with broad oval leaves that turn clear yellow in autumn, ultimately reaching a size well beyond many other intermedia cultivars. Give it moist, humus-rich, slightly acidic soil in partial shade to full sun and generous lateral space to develop its full rounded form. Little pruning is needed beyond removing crossing or damaged wood after flowering.

common_name: Glowing Embers Witch Hazel (Spreading Burnt-Orange Winter Shrub)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, humus-rich, neutral to slightly acidic soil in partial shade to full sun; 'Glowing Embers' spreads wider than it grows tall, so site it where its low, broad silhouette has room to develop.

directions: Glowing Embers produces curled, crimped, burnt-orange strap petals with red tints emerging from a deep purplish-red calyx, opening as early as February whenever temperatures climb above freezing and curling shut again during hard cold snaps. It forms a broad, spreading shrub with rounded, maroon-tinted young foliage that matures to dark green before turning yellow in fall, and the early flowers are a valuable nectar source for foraging bees. Grow in neutral to slightly acidic, humus-rich soil in sun to partial shade, and prune only lightly after flowering to maintain its naturally horizontal branching habit.

common_name: Coombe Wood Chinese Witch Hazel (Historic Golden-Yellow Fragrant Selection)

planting.note: Plant container or balled stock in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, slightly acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade to full sun; 'Coombe Wood' is one of the oldest named Chinese witch hazel selections, identified at Kew around 1898 from a plant growing unrecognized at the Coombe Wood nursery.

directions: Coombe Wood bears dense clusters of golden-yellow, crinkled, ribbon-like petals with an orange-toned center, opening in mid- to late winter and carrying a strong, sweet fragrance that is among the most pronounced in the species. It grows into a large, spreading shrub with rounded leaves that color yellow in autumn, historically distinguished from the typical Chinese witch hazel by its richer flower color and more compact clustering of blooms. Plant in moist, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in partial shade to full sun, sheltered from harsh winter winds, and allow ample room for its eventual broad, multi-stemmed spread. It requires only minimal corrective pruning once established.

common_name: Aimelie Witch Hazel (Purple-Orange Petaled Burgundy-Calyx Winter Shrub)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, humus-rich, slightly acidic soil in full sun to partial shade; 'Aimelie' traces to the influential de Belder witch hazel breeding line and flowers earlier in mild climates than in colder ones.

directions: Aimelie carries unusual purple-toned orange petals radiating from a deep burgundy calyx, giving a smokier, more muted flower color than the typical clear orange or red intermedia cultivars. Bloom timing varies with climate, starting as early as February in milder regions and stretching into April farther north, with a light sweet fragrance on calm days. The shrub develops a rounded, multi-stemmed habit and tolerates both moist and moderately dry soils once established. Site it in full sun to partial shade for the best flower color and fall foliage display.

common_name: Antoine Kort Witch Hazel (Vigorous Clear-Red Fragrant Winter Shrub)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or spring in moderately fertile, well-drained, neutral to acidic soil in an open but sheltered site; 'Antoine Kort' grows into a large, spreading small tree form, so allow generous width as well as height.

directions: Antoine Kort is a vigorous, large-growing witch hazel selection bearing curled, strap-shaped, clear red petals set against a contrasting purple calyx, with a notably strong, sweet fragrance for a red-flowered cultivar. New spring foliage emerges with a bronzy-purple flush before turning glossy dark green for summer, then coloring yellow and orange in fall. It ultimately forms a spreading, small-tree-like shrub wider than it is tall, so it suits open sites where its mature silhouette can be appreciated. Grow in moderately fertile, well-drained, neutral to acidic soil, sheltered from strong wind but not deep shade.

common_name: Sandra Ozark Witch Hazel (Purple-New-Growth Gold-Tipped Orange-Flowered Native Selection)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist to moderately moist, slightly acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade to full sun; 'Sandra' is chosen as much for its purple-flushed spring foliage and fiery fall color as for its very early winter flowers.

directions: Sandra is a large, upright, vase-shaped selection of the native Ozark witch hazel, bearing bright orange, gold-tipped, narrow strap petals with a red-tinted base and a maroon-red calyx that open on bare stems in late winter with a sweet fragrance. Its new spring foliage emerges with a distinctive purple flush before settling to green for summer, then turns a striking butter-yellow suffused with orange-red in fall, giving the cultivar multi-season interest beyond its flowers. Plant in moist, slightly acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade to full sun, and expect good cold hardiness and tolerance of the rocky, streambank conditions typical of its native range. Minimal pruning is needed beyond shaping after flowering.
